statement: What is the last digit of 1¹ + 2² + 3³ + 4⁴ + 5⁵ + 6⁶ + 7⁷ + 8⁸ + 9⁹ + 10¹⁰?

choices.misconception: I thought an odd power of 7 always ends in 7, but 7⁷ ends in 3.
I thought an odd power of 3 always ends in 3, but 3³ = 27 ends in 7.
I assumed each term ends in the same digit as its base, so I added 1 + 2 + ... + 9 + 0 = 45.
I thought every power of 9 ends in 1, but odd powers of 9, such as 9⁹, end in 9.

hints: Only the last digit of each term matters.
Find the last digit of each power using the repeating cycle of last digits for its base, then add those ten digits and take the last digit of the total.
The cycles: 2 goes 2, 4, 8, 6; 3 goes 3, 9, 7, 1; 7 goes 7, 9, 3, 1; 8 goes 8, 4, 2, 6; 4 and 9 alternate between two digits.

solutions.reliable: Work out each last digit: 1¹ ends in 1, 2² = 4, 3³ = 27 ends in 7, 4⁴ = 256 ends in 6, 5⁵ ends in 5, 6⁶ ends in 6, 7⁷ ends in 3 (the cycle 7, 9, 3, 1 at position 3), 8⁸ ends in 6 (the cycle 8, 4, 2, 6 at position 4), 9⁹ ends in 9 (odd power), 10¹⁰ ends in 0. The sum of these digits is 1 + 4 + 7 + 6 + 5 + 6 + 3 + 6 + 9 + 0 = 47, so the last digit is 7. The transferable idea: last digits of powers repeat in short cycles, so only the exponent's position in the cycle matters.

whyOnTest: Last-digit questions test the cycles of powers, and each wrong choice comes from one plausible slip in a single cycle.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
